pins.title: Masking vs Blocking: How a White Noise Machine Helps Light Sleepers With Sudden Noises
pins.subtitle: Steady sound vs doors, sirens, snoring
pins.description: A sound machine doesn't remove noise from the room. It masks sudden, variable sounds like a car door, a siren, or a partner's snoring with a steady one that's easier for your brain to filter out. That's why a constant tone without loops or gaps tends to suit light sleepers. Compare a mechanical fan, a digital white noise machine, and a smart sound machine in the full guide. Not medical advice. #whitenoise #soundmachine #lightsleeper #sleeptips

pins.title: Light Sleeper's Sound Machine Checklist: Marpac Dohm, LectroFan, or Hatch Restore?
pins.subtitle: 4 questions before you pick
pins.description: Notice loop points in digital sound? A real-fan machine like the Marpac Dohm avoids them. Want more tones without smart features? LectroFan. Struggling with the wake-up too? Hatch Restore adds a sunrise light and app routines, but it's app-controlled. Sensitive to light as well? Check whether the display or night light can go dark. Not medical advice. #soundmachine #whitenoisemachine #lightsleeper #marpacdohm #hatchrestore

pins.title: Who a White Noise Machine Won't Help: Check This Before You Buy
pins.subtitle: Noise isn't always the problem
pins.description: Sound machines mask noise. They don't address sleep disruption from pain, anxiety, sleep apnea, or an irregular schedule. If a couple of weeks brings no improvement, noise may not be the main issue; look at light, temperature, and timing, and talk to a healthcare provider if disrupted sleep is ongoing. Keep the volume low for young children and follow the manufacturer's guidance. Not medical advice. #whitenoise #soundmachine #sleephygiene #lightsleeper
